title: Encrypted control plane for notifications and sensitive browser request/result flows

actors.name: authenticated_signer
actors.role: browser-side requester that signs and encrypts sensitive operations

actors.name: bahia_service
actors.role: service pubkey owner that decrypts requests, authorizes operations, dispatches handlers, and publishes encrypted results

actors.name: encrypted_request_relays
actors.role: relay set explicitly configured for encrypted browser request/result traffic

description: This slice covers the signer-first encrypted browser request/result transport used for sensitive operations, with notifications as the primary product vertical. It includes system discovery requirements, relay selection rules, request construction, publish/result correlation behavior, backend decrypt/authorize/dispatch behavior, and notification channel/log operations built on that transport.
in_scope: `/api/v1/system/info` fields required for encrypted browser operations: `nostr.service_pubkey`, `nostr.browser_encrypted_request_relays`, and the effective encrypted capability gate used by frontend stores
negative behavior for unavailable encrypted transport, publish rejection, decrypt failure, unauthorized requester, and terminal error results
out_of_scope: public signer-first command families for services, deployments, policies, and artifacts
REST compatibility behavior except where it helps define the boundary of this slice
org/member/invite and payment-history encrypted domains beyond acknowledging that they share the same transport family
relay-sidecar readable-kind policy for public operator flows
Soul Factory and LLM control-plane behavior
preconditions: The browser has an authenticated signer capable of signing and encrypting requests
`/api/v1/system/info` advertises a valid Bahia service pubkey and at least one `browser_encrypted_request_relays` URL
The encrypted transport is enabled in the current deployment topology and the backend is subscribed to the encrypted request kind family
The requesting pubkey is allowed to invoke the targeted encrypted operation
postconditions: Sensitive notification operations complete without publishing payloads to public browser relay URLs
The requester receives either a correlated encrypted success result or a correlated encrypted terminal error result
Frontend store state is updated only from decrypted result payloads or explicit local error handling

happy_paths.title: Load notification channels through encrypted request/result transport
steps: Frontend checks encrypted request availability from current system info
Frontend publishes encrypted request event with operation `notifications.channels.list`
Backend decrypts, authorizes, dispatches the notification list handler, and publishes a correlated encrypted result
Frontend decrypts the result and populates notification channel state

happy_paths.title: Create, update, test, delete, and list logs for notification channels over encrypted transport
steps: Frontend issues encrypted operations for channel create/update/test/delete and log retrieval
Backend dispatches the matching encrypted notification handlers
Frontend updates local channel/log state from decrypted payloads

failure_paths.title: Encrypted transport unavailable before publish
failure_paths.behavior: If system discovery does not advertise a service pubkey plus encrypted-request relays, the frontend store must fail locally and not publish any request

failure_paths.title: Publish rejected by all encrypted-request relays
failure_paths.behavior: If no relay returns an accepted OK, the request fails and the caller receives the rejection reason

failure_paths.title: Decrypt failure on backend
failure_paths.behavior: Malformed or undecryptable encrypted requests yield a correlated encrypted terminal error result with a decrypt-failure code

failure_paths.title: Unauthorized requester
failure_paths.behavior: A requester pubkey not authorized for the encrypted domain receives a correlated encrypted terminal error result and the handler is not invoked

failure_paths.title: Encrypted terminal result error
failure_paths.behavior: If the backend returns a terminal error payload, the frontend surfaces the error message rather than silently treating the request as successful

edge_cases: Correlated result filtering must ignore mismatched `#e`, mismatched `#p`, and spoofed authors
Duplicate result events must not cause duplicate resolution of the same request
Public browser relay URLs must not be treated as encrypted-request relay URLs even if they are present in system info
non_functional_requirements: Sensitive browser operations must not leak plaintext payloads onto public browser relays
Request/result correlation must be explicit and deterministic via request event id and requester pubkey
The transport must unsubscribe/clean up subscriptions after terminal success or failure
The transport must propagate publish rejection and terminal error details clearly to callers
dependencies: Encrypted request/result transport code in frontend and backend
Notification encrypted handlers and store operations

ambiguities.note: The encrypted operation catalog is not documented as comprehensively as the public control-plane families; notifications are well-evidenced, but other encrypted domains share the transport with less explicit narrative coverage.

The slice is clear on browser encrypted-request relays versus public browser relays, but end-to-end relay topology verification is currently stronger in unit tests and docs than in selected browser E2E evidence.

human_decisions: Should the encrypted operation catalog be promoted to a first-class normative table alongside public command families?
Should encrypted-domain browser journeys receive explicit E2E coverage as a release gate, or is unit/backend transport coverage sufficient for this slice?
